Name: Thomas Cranmer
Summary: Archbishop of Canterbury (1489-1556) under Henry VIII and Edward VI, who steered the English church toward Reformed doctrine and an English-language liturgy.
Contribution: He compiled the Book of Common Prayer, putting congregational worship, Scripture reading, and the Lord's Supper into the people's own language, and he framed the Forty-Two Articles that became the basis of Anglican doctrine. His liturgy still shapes Anglican worship worldwide.
KeyWorks: Book of Common Prayer; Forty-Two Articles
Testimony: Under Mary I he was condemned for heresy and, after a period of recantation under pressure, publicly withdrew his recantations before being burned at the stake in Oxford.
